'''Nar Shaddaa wind chimes''' were a type of traditional, wind-activated musical instrument constructed by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. They consisted of several metallic cylinders hanging on fine threads, in the middle of which would hang a Hutt-shaped piece of flattened metal. The wind caused the Hutt shape to move and waver, hitting the chimes and thus producing a metallic noise. The Nar Shaddaa wind chimes were a symbol of renewal in Hutt society.<ref name="CCG" />

[[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], the [[Kajidii/Legends|kajidii]] of the [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijic]] clan, possessed a set of such windchimes, made of four tubes.<ref name="RotJ" /> That set was among the few possessions that Jabba brought with him when he moved the headquarters of his [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|criminal empire]] from Nar Shaddaa<ref name="CCG" /> to the [[Star/Legends|sun]]-scorched [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[516 BBY]]. The Hutt had a [[Throne/Legends|throne room]] built in the subterranean level of a former [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|monastery]] of the [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr Order]], which became his [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]].<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> The crime lord's wind chime was hung in the archway of the main entrance to the throne room.<ref name="RotJ" /> It was still hanging there in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> but Jabba's [[Death/Legends|assassination]] that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]] caused the palace and all it contained to fall into abandonment.<ref name="RotJ" />
